title: Style as a Confound: False Positives in AI Detection of Non-Native Academic Writing
abstract: arXiv:2608.26710v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI text detectors are increasingly employed in academic settings, but it remains unclear whether their outputs reflect AI authorship itself or broader linguistic features associated with polished academic English. Previous studies have reported high false-positive rates (FPRs) for non-native English writing, but population-level comparisons confound authorship with differences in topic, domain, and writing style. Professional editing provides a useful setting for examining this issue because it changes the linguistic form of manuscripts while preserving authorship and content. We examined 135,389 document pairs from a professional English editing service (2018-2025), comprising non-native manuscripts and their native-edited versions, to assess how editing affects detector responses controlling for content and authorship. translated_title: 风格作为混杂因素：非母语学术写作中AI检测的误报问题
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26710v1 公告类型：新 摘要：AI文本检测器在学术环境中的应用日益增多，但其输出结果是否真正反映AI作者身份，还是仅仅反映了与润色后的学术英语相关的更广泛语言特征，目前尚不明确。先前研究已报告非母语英语写作存在较高的误报率（FPRs），但群体层面的比较将作者身份与主题、领域和写作风格的差异混淆在一起。专业编辑提供了一个有用的研究场景，因为它改变了手稿的语言形式，同时保留了作者身份和内容。我们检查了来自一家专业英语编辑服务的135,389对文档（2018-2025年），包括非母语手稿及其母语编辑版本，以评估编辑如何影响检测器响应，同时控制内容和作者身份。对于13种AI文本检测器，人类撰写文本的误报率差异很大，从0.0%到100.0%不等。响应在不同检测器间存在差异。
tldr: 本研究通过135,389对专业编辑前后的非母语论文对比，发现AI检测器的误报率受写作风格影响显著，且不同检测器差异极大（0%至100%），表明风格是导致误报的关键混杂因素。
en_tdlr: This study, using 135,389 pairs of non-native manuscripts before and after professional editing, reveals that AI detector false-positive rates are significantly influenced by writing style, varying widely across detectors (0% to 100%), indicating style as a key confounding factor in false positives.
